blocks.text: Granville, in the City of Richmond, is a real estate board name for streets along Granville Avenue, which runs east–west from the Middle Arm and the Richmond Olympic Oval through City Centre and Broadmoor toward Garden City and beyond. It is not a standalone official Area Plan. Minoru Park and Brighouse Station sit on the City Centre stretch of this street.

Homes for sale in Granville include apartments closer to City Centre and the Oval, and houses or townhouses on the mid-city blocks farther east and west. The Oval’s waterfront dike path and the Minoru civic campus are the main recreation points on the west end of the avenue.

blocks.text: Current listings name the building "FORM by Anthem," place it in Fairview VW / South Granville, and record year built 2026, Apartment/Condo, with cats OK in the listing pet field. As a 2026 building, early sales carry new-build GST.

Listing copy describes "PINTURA, a boutique concrete building by Intracorp" in South Granville/Fairview; a listing records year built 2005, Apartment/Condo, concrete construction, and describes the building as "rental and pet friendly." A townhouse component also carries the Pintura name at 1576 West 8th Avenue (see the townhome subsection).

Listings call the building "Landmark Sunset" in Fairview, close to the South Granville shops. One listing gives 1976 as the year built, wood frame with stucco, while a building directory says 1978 and says its bylaws include "Pets allowed, rentals allowed".
Streets, schools and getting around Granville

items.t: South Granville is a recognised smaller area of the city but not one of the City's 22 distinct local areas; the corridor runs through the Fairview local area, with the Shaughnessy local area at its south end. The South Granville Business Improvement Association district runs along Granville Street from the Granville Bridge to 16th Avenue; the residential side streets run east toward Oak Street and west toward Burrard Street.

The condos are on the residential side streets on either side of Granville (West 6th, West 8th and West 14th Avenues between Burrard or Fir and Oak), not on Granville Street's shopping strip. Those same streets have many purpose-built rental buildings, so a lot of the "apartment buildings" here aren't condos at all.

Landmarks and retail: Gallery Row (the art-gallery stretch of the South Granville shopping district), the Stanley Theatre at 2750 Granville Street (650 seats, opened 1931 as a cinema and vaudeville house), Granville Park at 3001 Fir Street, and Vancouver General Hospital at 899 West 12th Avenue a few blocks east.

Transit: the corridor is bus-served today, including the 99 B-Line on West Broadway; the Broadway Subway — the 5.7 km Millennium Line extension with six underground stations including South Granville Station — is scheduled to enter service in fall 2027.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Granville

items.t: Area plan — the Broadway Plan: the Plan covers Clark Drive to Vine Street and 1st to 16th Avenues, was approved June 22, 2022 and updated in December 2024, and provides for a South Granville Station area with buildings up to 30–40 storeys near the station (40-storey maximum in the Granville/Burrard Slopes – Area A policy). Every building sits inside the Plan area — but the Plan is policy, not zoning: most higher-density forms still require rezoning. Citywide direction otherwise comes from the Vancouver Official Development Plan, which replaced the Vancouver Plan on March 31, 2026.

The blocks that look densest have the least to buy. The South Granville Apartment District, roughly West 11th to West 16th Avenues from Fir to Birch, is one of the city's only intact pre-war apartment neighbourhoods, and its buildings are rentals. The strata buildings are on the quieter avenues north and south of it.

Pintura is two products under one name. The West 8th Avenue development carries both apartment condos (1530 West 8th Avenue) and concrete townhouses (1576 West 8th Avenue) — a "Pintura" listing must be matched by address and type before it is compared.

The heritage apartment buildings carry two addresses each. Douglas Lodge is both 1507–1509 West 12th Avenue and 2799 Granville Street; Crescent Court is both 1504–1512 West 14th Avenue and 3003–3007 Granville Street — a search on one address alone gives a half picture of the same building.

The hospital is the corridor's quiet anchor tenant. Vancouver General Hospital, 899 West 12th Avenue — BC's referral centre for many provincial programs and a teaching hospital — sits a few blocks east of Granville Street, which is a structural source of both owner and renter demand on the side streets.

items.t: For Pintura's townhouses, or any strata here, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. Here, the Form B is also the quickest way to confirm a building is strata at all; the rental buildings don't have one. Rental and pet lines in listings aren't the bylaws.
Fee-simple side-street houses: The Heritage project's three houses are designated protected heritage property — heritage rules ride on top of whichever tenure title shows.
Extra units: on the side streets, the R1-1 zone's rules for suites, laneway houses and multiplexes of up to 6 units (or 8 rentals) are what set lot values.

Plan — the Broadway Plan: the Plan covers Clark Drive to Vine Street and 1st to 16th Avenues, was approved by Council on June 22, 2022 and updated in December 2024, and provides for a South Granville Station area with buildings up to 30–40 storeys near the station (40-storey maximum in the Granville/Burrard Slopes – Area A station-area policy). Every address sits inside the Plan area — but the Plan is policy, not zoning: most higher-density forms still require rezoning, and purpose-built rental buildings in the corridor carry tenant-relocation implications under the Plan's renter protections. Citywide direction otherwise comes from the Vancouver Official Development Plan, which replaced the Vancouver Plan on March 31, 2026.

items.t: The station is dated, not rumoured. The Broadway Subway's South Granville Station is scheduled to enter service in fall 2027 on the Province's published date — corridor pricing already trades on that date, so a buyer should underwrite to it rather than to "someday."

Fairview was named in 1886 by CPR Land Commissioner L.A. Hamilton, whose survey established the numbered east–west avenues and named the cross streets after trees — which is why the corridor's townhouse addresses read as tree names (Fir, Birch, Hemlock) between Granville and Oak. Less than 100 years ago the False Creek and Fairview Slopes area was a forest of huge fir trees.

Side-street house lots: detached houses and character homes on the quieter side streets of Fairview and the upper Shaughnessy edge, with low-rise and mid-rise condo and rental apartment buildings lining Granville Street and West Broadway. A fee-simple lot carries no strata, no Form B and no strata fees.

Lot character: side-street house lots are governed by the R1-1 schedule where it applies (minimum site areas from 306 m² by form — 306 m² for a single detached house or duplex and for a multiple dwelling of 3 to 4 units, 464 m² for 5 units, 557 m² for 6 to 8 units); By-law No. 13817 amended the Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575 to replace the old RS districts with R1-1, allowing up to 6 strata units, or up to 8 secured rental units, on former single-family lots, subject to the district schedule's site standards. The Granville Street frontage itself sits under commercial / mixed-use districts.
Serviced position: corridor homes are on City water and sewer services.
Flood position: the corridor's north end sits above the False Creek shoreline.

Historic subdivisions = built lot fabric, not offerings: Fairview was named in 1886 by CPR Land Commissioner L.A. Hamilton, whose survey established the numbered east–west avenues and named the cross streets after trees — the side-street lot fabric is that historic survey, fully built, not an offering.

Broadway Plan station ground: the Broadway Plan covers Clark Drive to Vine Street and 1st to 16th Avenues (approved June 22, 2022; updated December 2024) and provides for a South Granville Station area with buildings up to 30–40 storeys near the station — a 40-storey maximum in the Granville/Burrard Slopes – Area A station-area policy. The Plan is a policy framework, not a rezoning: most higher-density forms still require rezoning, and purpose-built rental buildings in the corridor carry tenant-relocation implications under the Plan's renter protections. No lot is presented as rezoned, assembled or for sale on this basis.

Land values are highest on the residential side streets on either side of Granville (West 6th, West 8th and West 14th Avenues between Burrard or Fir and Oak) and around the Granville and Broadway station. Granville Street's shopping strip is commercial and mixed-use zoning. The same side streets have many purpose-built rental buildings, so a lot of the "apartment buildings" here aren't strata.

Transit: the corridor is bus-served today, including the 99 B-Line along West Broadway; the Broadway Subway — the 5.7 km Millennium Line extension with six new underground stations including South Granville Station — is scheduled to enter service in fall 2027.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Granville

items.t: Zoning — Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575, R1-1 (side streets, via By-law No. 13817) + commercial / mixed-use (frontage): R1-1 allows up to 6 strata units, or up to 8 secured rental units, on former single-family lots, subject to the district schedule (306 m² / 464 m² / 557 m² minimum site areas by form; secondary suite and laneway house with a house). The Granville Street frontage sits under commercial / mixed-use districts; a corridor strata example, The Avedon, is recorded in its listing as zoned RM-3.

Plans: the Broadway Plan (Clark Drive to Vine Street, 1st to 16th Avenues; approved June 22, 2022 and updated December 2024) sets heights around the stations, but it's policy, not zoning. City-wide direction otherwise comes from the Vancouver Official Development Plan, which replaced the Vancouver Plan on March 31, 2026. Don't price a lot on tower density until you know what the zoning allows.

Heritage: the three Sixteenth & Burrard houses are designated heritage property, and Douglas Lodge and Crescent Court are on the City's Heritage Register. Heritage rules apply regardless of ownership type, and character-home rules need checking before promoting a side-street lot's development potential.

Strata rules (for the strata buildings, and any bare-land strata lot): check the Form B (fees, amounts owing, levies, contingency reserve balance and insurance; within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page); here it's also the quickest way to confirm a building is strata, since the rental buildings don't have one. Stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years, and at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve. Rental bans are void (short-term rentals can still be limited), and the only valid age bylaw is 55 and older, with exemptions for a younger spouse or partner, caregivers, existing residents and some children, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable.

faq.a: The downtown entertainment corridor is a different market and none of its buildings appear here.

Because they're purpose-built rentals owned as whole buildings: The Leeward is a 48-suite rental tower (1968) and Santa Monica a 13-suite rental building (1929), and the district from West 11th to 16th and Fir to Birch is an intact pre-war rental apartment neighbourhood. A building being on the Heritage Register (Douglas Lodge, Crescent Court) doesn't mean it's a strata.
